To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the social sciences use multi-agent systems primarily for the analysis of social systems, whereas computer science uses them for synthesis, i.e., for the design of systems; (2) the social sciences tend to be more concerned with sufficiency, i.e., the extent to which a model can be used to explain a phenomenon, whereas computer science is more concerned with necessity, i.e., whether a model is capable of generating the phenomenon in question; (3) there are some important differences

the social sciences use multi-agent systems to explain and understand social phenomena; that computer science uses them to design and build social phenomena; and that both fields use them to study sufficiency and necessity.

1) the distinction between analysis and synthesis is important for the use of multi-agent systems in social science; 2) the use of multiagent systems is not limited to the social sciences; and 3) the use of ACE is not limited to analysis or synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of social structures and institutions, and the analysis of the social structures and institutions we observe.
the use of multi-agent systems to model and explain social phenomena.
the analysis of social systems, not their synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social sciences are more interested in using ACE as tools for analysis than in using them as a basis for building systems.
the uses of multi-agents in the social sciences are as diverse as the sciences themselves.
the uses of multi agent systems are not only complementary but also mutually reinforcing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we use agent based computational models to understand the emergence and evolution of social order.
ACE is a useful method of analysis, and that it is a promising tool for design.
we are interested in the analysis of multi-agent systems, and that we are interested primarily in the social sciences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multi-agent systems can be used for analysis and synthesis in the social sciences, but the uses of these systems are not interchangeable.
the social science uses are not just a subset of the computer science uses, and vice versa.
, although multi-agent systems are not a panacea, they can be a valuable tool in both social science research and computer science design.
